_comment: SYNTHETIC EXAMPLE - invented bibliography. Authors, journals, years, DOIs and abstracts are fabricated for interface demonstration only.

references.title: TemplateTransfer: ligand binding-site prediction by single-template pocket transplantation
references.abstract: TemplateTransfer predicts ligand binding sites by transplanting pockets from the single highest-identity template structure. On an invented benchmark of 80 targets it reaches 0.55 top-1 pocket precision when template identity exceeds 40%, but precision drops to 0.41 for targets below 30% identity, because a single template often carries a partially mismatched pocket.

references.title: SeqPocket: sequence-only binding-site prediction with a residue-attention network
references.abstract: SeqPocket predicts binding residues directly from sequence using a residue-attention network, requiring no structural template. It matches template-based methods on targets with no usable template but lags them by 0.10 top-1 precision on template-rich targets. The authors note it cannot localize pockets that lack sequence motifs.

references.title: MultiTempl: naive pocket pooling from multiple templates
references.abstract: MultiTempl pools predicted pockets from up to 8 template structures and ranks them by pocket frequency. Pooling raises recall by 0.15 over single-template transfer, but precision on low-identity targets stays flat because low-quality templates vote with equal weight.

references.title: GeoScore: geometry-based ranking of candidate binding pockets
references.abstract: GeoScore ranks candidate pockets by geometric descriptors (depth, enclosure, hydrophobic patch area) without any template. It is fast and template-free, but the abstract reports no comparison against template-based predictors and no low-identity evaluation.

references.title: ConsenSite: consensus scoring of pockets across homologous structures
references.abstract: ConsenSite scores candidate pockets by unweighted consensus across homologous experimental structures of the same protein. It improves precision by 0.07 over single-structure scoring, but requires multiple experimental structures of the target itself, which are unavailable for most prediction targets; it was not evaluated on template-based transfer.

references.title: A survey of binding-site prediction methods
references.abstract: This survey groups binding-site predictors into template-based, geometry-based and sequence-based families, and observes that low-identity template transfer remains the weakest setting across all template-based methods surveyed.
